title: Spatial Orientation Shrinks and Expands Psychological Distance

triggers: spatial orientation toward away psychological distance construal level

claims.statement: Study 1 (n = 202, Bay St. subway): orientation x station interaction F(3,194) = 16.28, eta_p^2 = .20; station main effect F = 24.10; no orientation main effect (F < 1). Stations in the direction of travel feel closer (simple effects p < .001, .001, .053, < .001).
claims.scope: Toronto subway riders, 1-7 rating, one item, between-subjects, ~25 per cell.

quantities.name: s1_toward_minus_away_rating
quantities.baseline: OLS with station side and near/far; p < 1e-7; Mann-Whitney toward vs away p = 2.0e-7

our_assessment.why: Every number reproduces from the deposit to the printed digit. The simple-effect eta_p^2 values are from separate per-station one-way ANOVAs (not the pooled error term) -- reproducible, but the paper does not say so. Recoded as the theoretically relevant contrast (toward vs away), the effect is 1.1 scale points and survives a rank test at p = 2e-7. This is the strong study of the paper.

claims.statement: Study 2 (n = 80, Christie station): direction of travel, not direction faced, drives subjective distance to the U of T campus: orientation F(1,76) = 4.79, p = .032, eta_p^2 = .06 (M 3.63 vs 4.15); facing and interaction Fs < 1.
claims.scope: 20 per cell, one item, one target location.

quantities.name: s2_orientation_F_reproduced
quantities.baseline: published 4.79, p .0318; Mann-Whitney p = .043; Welch p = .030; M east 3.625 printed 3.63

our_assessment.why: Reproduces exactly and survives a rank test, but it is one target at n = 80 with p = .03: weak evidence by itself, and its job (ruling out facing direction) rests on two null Fs at 20 per cell.

claims.statement: Study 3a (n = 100, one intersection): a sale was judged to have happened more recently at the drugstore participants walked toward (M = 7.65 min, SD 9.98) than at the one behind them (14.83, 17.19), F(1,98) = 6.65, p = .011.
claims.scope: All participants faced east; condition = which store was named, so orientation is confounded with store identity (the authors say so).

quantities.name: s3a_F_recomputed
quantities.baseline: published 6.65; M toward 7.67 vs printed 7.65 (a one-minute difference in one of 52 values); log1p p = .0077; Mann-Whitney p = .0075

our_assessment.why: Reproduces to within one data unit and is robust to the heavy right skew (rank and log tests p < .01). The design cannot separate orientation from store; Study 3b was built to fix that.

claims.statement: Study 3b (n = 86, Vancouver): crossing orientation with target store, a wrong drink order was judged more recent at the store walked toward (14.36 vs 25.43 min), F(1,82) = 6.86, p = .011; no effect of target (F < 1), no interaction (p > .18).
claims.scope: 2 x 2 between-subjects, 20-22 per cell; minutes estimate, heavy right tail (max 120).

our_assessment.why: The headline F reproduces exactly, but it is carried by the tail: the away condition holds the 120-minute answer and a rank test gives p = .11. 'F < 1' for target is false under every sum-of-squares type (1.48-1.77) -- small in consequence (p ~ .19) but a reported number that is not what the data give.

claims.statement: Study 4 (n = 50, Bloor-Yonge): riders heading toward the lottery-draw location judged a jackpot win more likely (M 4.00 vs 2.80), F(1,48) = 6.09, p = .017; familiarity r = -.343, p = .02; ANCOVA p = .009.

quantities.name: s4_F_reproduced
quantities.baseline: published 6.09; familiarity r p = .0148 printed '.02'; ANCOVA p .0090 = .009; Mann-Whitney p = .016

our_assessment.why: Reproduces and survives a rank test. The p for r is .0148 and is printed as .02 (rounding error, harmless in direction). Single item, n = 50.

claims.statement: Study 5 (n = 45, mall): a traveller described as departing for (toward) rather than arriving from Chicago felt more similar (M 2.41 vs 1.61), F(1,43) = 4.03, p = .051; presented as 'a similar pattern of results'.
claims.scope: 22/23 per cell; 26 of 45 answers are 1 on a 1-7 scale.

quantities.name: s5_F_reproduced
quantities.baseline: published 4.03, p .0509; Mann-Whitney p = .068; Welch p = .054; 16/23 'arriving' answers at the floor (1)

our_assessment.why: p = .051 at n = 45 on a floor-bound item is counted by the General Discussion as support for the fourth dimension. The data neither establish nor exclude the effect; the abstract reports it as a finding.

claims.statement: Taken as a set, the five cross-dimension tests (Studies 2, 3a, 3b, 4, 5; p = .032, .012, .011, .017, .051) are more homogeneous than independent studies allow: var(z) = 0.067 (expected >= 1), TIVA p = .008; Monte Carlo under the pooled effect with no selection p = .0064; joint power at the pooled d = 0.56 is 0.086; probability that all five land in (.01, .06) under that world .00095.
claims.scope: Set chosen by me after reading the paper as the tests that carry the cross-dimension claim (Study 1 excluded: different, spatial claim, and much stronger). Including Study 1 gives var(z) = 1.44, no flag.

quantities.name: tiva_var_z_five_cross_dimension_tests
quantities.baseline: expected >= 1; left-tail chi2(4) p = 0.0082; MC p (no-selection world, 20,000 reps) = 0.0064

quantities.name: joint_power_at_pooled_effect
quantities.baseline: pooled d = 0.557 (fixed, from the five ps); at alpha .06: 0.109; at half the pooled d: 0.0007

our_assessment.why: The detector was calibrated before use: it flags 4.3% of honest sets at these ns and 78% of null file-drawer sets. The observed variance (0.067) is below the MEDIAN variance of the null-with-file-drawer world (0.084). This is evidence that the five reported tests are a selected subset of what was run (unreported studies, optional stopping -- 'collected data until that number was achieved' is a minimum, not a stopping rule -- or analysis choice). It is not evidence about which. The set was chosen post hoc; with Study 1 in, nothing flags.
